newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Emirates to double HK-Dubai cargo capacity in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Emirates to double HK-Dubai cargo capacity in Oct.

text.p: Dubai government-owned airline Emirates said it will double cargo capacity between Hong Kong and its Dubai hub when it introduces new Boeing 777 aircraft on the route later this year.

The route will become all-777 operated from October 1 offering up to 25 tonnes of bellyhold cargo capacity on each flight compared to around 12 tonnes on smaller Airbus aircraft currently used, the carrier's Hong Kong cargo manager Jacky Lau told Reuters.
Emirates currently offers seven flights a week between Hong Kong and Dubai, one of which is already 777-operated.
Emirates flights to Manila via Hong Kong will also be flown by 777s, Lau added.

Emirates also has an additional 110 tonnes of cargo capacity available on a twice-weekly freighter service from Hong Kong to Dubai and on to Amsterdam, offering same-day trucking connections to major European destinations.
Space on the Boeing 747-200 freighter, wet-leased from Atlas Air, is shared with KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, Lau said.
Last year, Emirates said it flew 13,000 tonnes of cargo out of Hong Kong to Dubai and onward to its European destinations including London, Paris and Manchester.
Lau said an estimated 8-9,000 tonnes of cargo was flown into Hong Kong, one quarter of that total bound for onward points.
Lau said he would be conducting a cargo sales drive in the territory to fill the extra capacity for both Middle East and European destinations.
"Our first priority is Europe-bound cargo and we are looking for as much of this to carry as we can. Any remaining space is dedicated to Middle East or African destinations," he said.
"The Middle East market, which offers us high-yield cargo, is very stable and does not fluctuate as much as the European market. The slack and peak seasons are not as wide," Lau added.
